title: Grateful Dead Live at Hartford Civic Center on 1982-04-18

ai_review.summary: A stellar soundboard recording of the 4‑18‑82 Hartford show captures a high‑energy performance highlighted by blistering Let It Grow, soaring Space and a knockout second set.
ai_review.review: The board capture is praised for its crisp, well‑balanced mix that lets every instrument shine, while the concert itself is described as a powerhouse night with an unstoppable second set. Standout moments include Jerry’s epic solo in “Let it Grow,” Phil’s spaced‑out “Space,” and a fiery run through Althea, Big Railroad Blues and Samson.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews award 4–5 stars and extol both the musical performance and the soundboard quality; recording issues are minor, giving a combined high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, well‑balanced and ‘amazing’; board mix praised for clarity. One comment notes an audience version sounds “underwater,” confirming the board is superior.

standout_songs: Playing in the Band > Eyes of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is solid and rocking, but the second set delivers the ‘meat of the show’ with seamless segues (e.g., Sugar Magnolia > Playin' > SSDD) and a high‑octane climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers call his solos “amazing,” especially the Let It Grow solo, noting he was ‘ripping’ throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for his “spaced out” Space jam and the famed “earthquake” vibe that shook the venue.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for strong vocals, rhythm work and slide on Samson; praised as a great rhythm guitarist.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s Hammond organ work is singled out on Big Railroad Blues and RxR Blues, described as ‘slashing’ and ‘ripping.’
band_member_comments.Drums: The Rhythm Devils receive nods for driving the high‑energy jams; no specific criticisms.
